criteria.reason: Explicitly recalls the earlier four-test approach and applies specificity, independent data, and fact/opinion separation; the source-interest test is only implicit.
Beyond 'unverifiable as stated', it rules the claim 'almost certainly not true', a substantive verdict resting partly on unverifiable citations.
Flags hidden assumptions (storage, imports, geography, timing) and separates slogan from checkable fact, though study findings are asserted as established fact.
Urges skepticism toward both camps' absolutes, but only the renewables claim receives a definitive negative verdict, creating asymmetric treatment.

position: Renewables-alone winter-supply claim almost certainly false
factual_errors: Presents an unverifiable JRC finding (100-200 TWh seasonal storage) as established fact.
summary: Reapplies the earlier scrutiny framework and flags assumptions well, but rejects the renewables claim more harshly than the nuclear claim, citing unverifiable studies as fact.
